title: EverMall: performance proofs - ramp plan & initial tests
text:
EverMall: performance proofs - ramp plan & initial tests

['From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Lila Chen <lila.chen@evermall.com>, ops@evermall.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: EverMall - performance proofs: ramp plan & initial test window

Hi Lila / Ops team –

Following our onboarding call, attaching a proposed run plan for the Proof-of-Performance (PoP) window. High-level goals we agreed:

- Targets: P95 generation latency < 300 ms, median < 120 ms.
- Throughput: sustained 300 requests/sec across the target route during peak emulation.
- Concurrency: scale test up to 120 concurrent sessions; tail latency (99th) should remain under 900 ms.
- Success criteria: no >3% error rate at target throughput; no sustained CPU/GPU >85% for >5 minutes.

Planned windows (PST):
- Preliminary smoke: Mon 2026-03-09 10:00–11:30
- Ramp & soak: Tue 2026-03-10 09:00–14:00

What we need from EverMall before the smoke test:
- A short-lived API key for test traffic (scoped to test environment) OR a load balancer endpoint we can push to.
- Location of the test dataset (S3 path) and a sample of the input payloads (we only need 200 examples for warmup).
- Allowlist for Redwood test IPs (I’ve included the list in the Drive doc).

Attachments: evermall-loadplan-v1.csv (traffic mix + concurrency steps). I’ve also uploaded a run script (redwood-run-script-v2.sh) to the shared Drive.

Please confirm windows and whether Monday smoke is still OK. If anything shifts we’ll adapt.

Thanks –
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

', 'From: Lila Chen <lila.chen@evermall.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EverMall - performance proofs: ramp plan & initial test window

Rishi –

Thanks for the plan. Monday smoke window works for us; Tue ramp looks fine as well. A few quick clarifications before we hand you test keys: 

- Which model variant will you run? (we have an internal preference for the 8-bit quantized variant to match staging).
- Will Redwood use token-level telemetry or only server-side metrics? We want to ensure PII is never logged.
- We’ll provide an S3 test bucket: s3://evermall-testing/llm-samples/ (200 samples added).

I’m looping ops@evermall.com here. Also attaching our recent internal NIC perf numbers that may be useful.

Lila Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, EverMall
lila.chen@evermall.com

', 'From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EverMall - performance proofs: ramp plan & initial test window

Quick internal note –

We should: 
- Run the smoke with the quantized-8b model (matches EverMall ask) and the unquantized 13b at lower qps to compare degradation patterns.
- Enable prefix/KV cache telemetry and a short token-sampling trace (no input payloads in traces) to verify cache hit rate.
- Provision a Grafana dashboard link for EverMall before the smoke so they can watch metrics.

I can take ownership of the smoke test orchestration on Monday and run the ramp on Tue. Karthik – please prepare the telemetry exporters and make sure logs are scrubbed of payloads.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com

', 'From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Lila Chen <lila.chen@evermall.com>, ops@evermall.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Kickoff: Monday smoke + pre-checks (EverMall PoP)

Lila / team –

We’re set to run the smoke test in ~55 minutes (start 10:00 PST). Quick checklist before we start: 

1) Test API key: evermall-test-2026 (temporary, expires 2026-03-11). Please confirm this key is active and scoped to staging only.
2) S3 samples: confirmed receipt of 200 examples at s3://evermall-testing/llm-samples/ (thanks).
3) IP allowlist: your infra team confirmed allowlist entries for 34.210.12.45 and 34.210.12.46?
4) Telemetry: Karthik enabled token-metrics exporter; Monica has dashboard link ready: https://drive.redwood.com/s/evermall-onboard/performance-plan#grafana

We’ll run 3 quick smoke stages: 
- Warmup (5 min): 10–30 qps
- Validation (10 min): 60 qps, concurrency 8
- Burst check (15 min): step to 150 qps

If smoke passes (no errors, tail below target), we’ll proceed to a short post-run artifact share. Attaching redwood-run-script-v2.sh for reference.

On Mon, 6 Mar 2026 at 08:15 Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick internal note –
> 
> We should: 
> - Run the smoke with the quantized-8b model (matches EverMall ask) and the unquantized 13b at lower qps to compare degradation patterns.
> - Enable prefix/KV cache telemetry and a short token-sampling trace (no input payloads in traces) to verify cache hit rate.
> - Provision a Grafana dashboard link for EverMall before the smoke so they can watch metrics.
> 
> Monica Patel

Thanks, starting in 10.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
', 'From: Lila Chen <lila.chen@evermall.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, ops@evermall.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Monday smoke + pre-checks (EverMall PoP)

Rishi / team –

Thanks for running the smoke. Summary from our side (attached run-results-20260309.zip and telemetry-pack-20260309.json):

- Warmup & validation steps succeeded. No errors during warmup.
- At the 150 qps burst we saw CPU saturation on our LB nodes and a spike in 99th latency to ~1.2s (above the 900 ms goal).
- Memory on the model nodes remained healthy; GPUs peaked at ~78%.
- We included a packet capture around the spike window; looks like a small retransmit storm on our infra side.

Next asks:
1) Can Redwood re-run the burst step but hold at 120 qps for 30 minutes and confirm stability?
2) Can you share the per-request trace sample for the 14:02–14:07 window (token-level sampling only, no payloads)?

We can join a short post-mortem sync Wed 2026-03-11 09:00 PST to review artifacts.

Lila Chen
Head of Platform Engineering | EverMall

', 'From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Lila Chen <lila.chen@evermall.com>, ops@evermall.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Monday smoke + pre-checks (EverMall PoP)

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the artifacts, Lila. We got the run-results-20260309.zip and telemetry bundle – thanks. Immediate next steps from Redwood: 

- We’ll re-run the burst stage at 120 qps for a 30-minute soak tomorrow morning (Wed 2026-03-11 09:00 PST). Monica will run orchestration; Karthik will pull the trace samples for the 14:02–14:07 window and redact payloads.
- I’ll also run a quick CPU/connection profile on our side to see if the retransmits align with any connection resets.
- Post-run we’ll upload: run-results-20260310-120qps.zip and a short runbook note describing any mitigation recommendations (LB tuning suggestions + connection timeout tweaks).

I’ll set the post-mortem invite for Wed 2026-03-11 09:30 PST to allow data ingest. If EverMall prefers 09:00 we can move it earlier.

Thanks –
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
']
